This synchrony between pubertal length and weight underscores an efficient resource allocation that minimizes time spent as a non-reproductive juvenile, allowing rapid transition to the adult stage.

The maximum recorded reproductive rate represents the peak output observed under optimal laboratory feeding regimes and likely reflects the physiological upper limit of vitellogenesis in this species. Field-caught ovigerous females typically display lower but sustained fecundity across successive spawning events, influenced by the interplay between food concentration and ambient temperature.

This maximum weight is matched exactly by the dry weight at puberty, also 31.8601 micrograms , strongly reinforcing the observation that body mass stabilizes at the onset of reproductive maturity.
